title: Partial sums of random completely multiplicative functions

problemStatement.formal: For Rademacher completely multiplicative f, study whether limsup_N |sum_{m<=N} f(m)|/sqrt(N)=infinity almost surely, alongside Atherfold's sqrt(N)(log N)^{1+o(1)} upper bound.
problemStatement.plain: This entry formalizes the partial-sum problem for random completely multiplicative functions. It defines Rademacher multiplicative functions, proves basic structural facts about their values and sums, states the Erdos 1144 growth conjecture, and records Atherfold's recent upper bound as an axiom.
whyMatters: Connects multiplicative number theory, probabilistic models, and growth rates of partial sums.
Clarifies which parts are elementary Lean work and which parts remain probabilistic analytic input.

proven: `partialSum_zero`, `partialSum_one`, `partialSum_two`, and `partialSum_succ` establish small-value and recurrence facts for partial sums.
`exists_linear_growth_rademacher` shows the all-ones Rademacher function has linear partial-sum growth, so Atherfold's bound is genuinely probabilistic.
`conjecture_and_atherfold_pinch` packages the conjectural lower growth together with the axiomatized Atherfold upper bound.
open: `atherfold_upper_bound` is an axiom, and the file does not construct the probability space for random multiplicative functions.
The current formal predicates encode a strong eventual lower-growth formulation; aligning them precisely with a limsup-almost-sure statement is future work.
knownResults.goal: Refine the probabilistic formulation and replace the Atherfold axiom only after the random-function measure model is available.
